ticket.title: Foundation audit: two documented invariants are broken suite-wide, and no crate but workspace has a multi-repo test
ticket.description:
PROGRESS 2026-11-10, two of the four owed tests paid and the register halved 4 -> 2 (miter a89a5a4, 36871f7).

PAID - storypole-cli (storypole ed38beb). The debt was real and the code was wrong: `config check --workspace` discovered members of the directory it was launched in, so inside a member it answered repositories: 1 and called that a workspace audit. A pass covering nothing is indistinguishable from a pass covering everything, and every existing test ran from a suite root. Two changes: `main` opened a store at the launch directory before dispatching any command, so config refused to run in a member at all - --workspace now runs before that and the local audit opens its own; and the resolution now walks up with Membership::containing to the declared suite, falling back to the launch directory when there is none so a lone repository still audits itself. Three tests run the built binary: from a member the answer is 2, from the root still 2, and alone still 1. The member test fails with repositories: 1 before the fix, which is the evidence.

NOT A FINDING - sawhorse-core. The register entry described a call that no longer exists: telemetry writes through gaugeblock_workspace::sink_path, which resolves the suite on the caller behalf, and the crate calls no discovery function at all. Removed rather than paid, because a register listing work nobody owes is read as permanent scenery. The behavioural test the entry wanted is filed as SH-10 (write from a member, assert the span lands in the SUITE outbox).

STILL OWED - two.
* benchwork-cli, GB-293: handlers.rs:187 and daemon/routes_telemetry.rs:57.
* rabbet-cli, GB-304: commands/ingest.rs:29. Investigated while doing the above, and there is a specific defect rather than a missing test: GaugeblockPaths::discover resolves through the GIT COMMON DIR, so from a member checkout it returns that member .gaugeblock and paths.outbox() is the member spool - empty, because telemetry centralises at the suite root (GB-338). sawhorse answers the same question with sink_path and gets the suite. Two resolutions of one question, disagreeing, is the class this epic is about; rabbet should use sink_path and the test should assert the suite outbox is the one read when the command runs in a member.

PROGRESS 2026-11-10, third of four paid and the register is down to ONE (miter 156f8b3).

PAID - rabbet-cli, and it was a defect rather than a missing test. `rabbet ingest` with no --spool resolved through GaugeblockPaths::discover, which resolves via the GIT COMMON DIR and therefore never leaves the checkout it runs in. Traces are written at the suite root (GB-338), so a member own spool is empty: from a member the command read nothing, ingested nothing, and exited zero. An empty corpus and a corpus that was never looked for produce the same silence, which is why it survived - the suite has one spool with content and it is not the one a member resolves to. Fixed in rabbet 3f8ba5d on a new gaugeblock_workspace::outbox_path (common abb7341), the sibling of the sink_path sawhorse already used; a repository with no suite above it keeps its own spool. Tests: 4 in common (two repositories in scope, including one that pins discover answer as STILL the member, because if the two ever agreed the distinction could not be tested) and 3 in rabbet-cli asking the same question from inside a member.

NOT A FINDING - sawhorse-core, removed earlier: no discovery call survives; telemetry goes through sink_path. Behavioural test deferred as SH-10.

STILL OWED - one. benchwork-cli (handlers.rs:187, daemon/routes_telemetry.rs:57), which the register names as GB-293, which is waiting on GB-356 attribution. It is the only entry left and it says what blocks it, which is the difference between a debt register and a list of things nobody intends to do.

COMPLETE 2026-11-10: all four owed tests are paid or shown not owed, and the multi-repo debt register is EMPTY (miter 3207ea0).

FINAL - benchwork-cli (benchwork 9592f2a, 54ffca2). Two defects behind one debt entry, both the same premise: the workspace is the repository I was launched in. The daemon tailed its telemetry through discover, which reports the checkout, while telemetry centralises at the suite root - so the panel said nothing yet while the log filled. And tidy --workspace discovered members of its launch directory, so from a member it walked target/ and worktrees, found zero repositories, and exited zero. Both fixed; three tests with two repositories in scope.

SCORE FOR THE EPIC, which is the argument for the gate rather than the instances: of four register entries, one was never a finding (sawhorse-core resolves through sink_path and calls no discovery function), and three were shipped defects rather than missing evidence - storypole config audit answering for the wrong repository, rabbet ingest reading an empty spool and exiting zero, benchwork tailing the wrong log and tidying zero repositories. Four of five defects found this way were wrong answers, not missing tests, which is exactly what the ticket predicted: with one repository in scope, per-repository logic and suite logic are indistinguishable.

The register is kept empty with its own instruction for re-adding: name the ticket that owes the test, and ask first whether the crate answer is wrong.

Remaining work is none on this epic. GB-293 is fixed and verified separately; GB-356 decided and partially wired; SH-10 is the one deferred test (telemetry written from a member lands in the suite outbox).

task.title: Foundation audit: two documented invariants are broken suite-wide, and no crate but workspace has a multi-repo test

acceptance_criteria:
AUDIT RUN 2026-11-06 across the seven foundation crates, plus the two invariants that cross repository boundaries. Two are broken, and one of them is the exact shape the workspace audit (GB-304) is looking for.

FOUNDATION HEALTH, measured (LOC, IO primitives, suite deps, stringified-error sites):
  crate                      LOC  fs proc env  gb-deps
  gaugeblock-contracts      1547   0    0   0        0
  gaugeblock-git             816   0    2   0        0
  gaugeblock-inventory      1039   6    1   1        1
  gaugeblock-mcp             473   0    0   0        0
  gaugeblock-security        610   0    0   0        0
  gaugeblock-syntax          272   0    0   0        1
  gaugeblock-workspace       632   5    0   3        2
That is healthier than expected. contracts does no IO and reads no clock or randomness, so its purity invariant holds. mcp holds no IO because it takes reader and writer, which is the right shape. security touching no environment variable is worth a second look later - a secret store that never reads env may be one that never gets a secret - but nothing there violates a written rule.

BROKEN INVARIANT 1 - one process boundary for git. SPEC.md says gaugeblock-git is the only crate that spawns git. It is not:
  outfeed/crates/outfeed-core/src/git/mod.rs:106      Command::new("git")
  outfeed/crates/outfeed-core/src/git/history.rs:41   Command::new("git")
The detail that makes this the interesting case: outfeed-core ALREADY depends on gaugeblock-git (its manifest line 14). So this is not a missing dependency that someone would notice - the crate has the foundation, and re-implemented a git call beside it anyway. That is precisely the 'depends on it' versus 'uses it fully' gap this audit exists to find, one crate lower down the stack than expected.
The remaining hits in the tree are test fixtures (miter's live under src/sandbox/tests/, which is test code despite the path), so the production code has exactly one legitimate spawner and two illegitimate ones.

BROKEN INVARIANT 2 - no tests can tell a repository from a suite. Multi-repository fixtures exist in exactly one crate:
  common/crates/gaugeblock-workspace   topology_fixture.rs, paths_fixture.rs
Nothing else in twelve repositories has a test where two repositories are in scope at once. This is the structural reason the three defects of the last two days reached production: benchwork tailing one telemetry log (GB-293), miter's dirty check blind to member repositories (GB-301), the index baseline written by no path that ran (GB-302). In each case every test had exactly one repository, and with one repository per-repository logic and suite logic are indistinguishable - so the tests passed and the code was wrong.

THE MIRRORING THESIS, which is why this audit is worth doing rather than chasing instances: these defects are not copy-paste. They are independently written from the same wrong premise ('the workspace is the repository I was launched in'), under time pressure, by work that optimises for the smallest diff that satisfies the ticket. Auditing one repository finds one instance; auditing the invariant finds the class. The four properties in GB-304 are the same method applied to paths; this ticket applies it to the git boundary and to test scope.

DURABLE MECHANISMS, in the order they pay off:
1. A test-scope rule: any crate that consumes WorkspaceTopology or GaugeblockPaths must have at least one test with two repositories in scope. Enforceable as a docs-check-style audit, and it is the single highest-value item here because it prevents the class rather than the instances.
2. A git-boundary gate: in production code (src/, excluding test directories) only gaugeblock-git may construct a git command. Same shape as the layers allowlist, with an allowlist for the foundation crate itself.
3. Fold 1 and 2 into whatever mechanism GB-304's gate ends up being, rather than shipping three audits.

NOT FIXED IN THIS PASS, deliberately. Moving outfeed's two git calls onto gaugeblock-git is small, but it is a separate atomic change in a crate this session has already restructured twice, and doing it here would bundle an unrelated edit into an audit commit.

ITEM 1 CLOSED 2026-11-06, commit 3053b30 (outfeed). The git process boundary holds again: the only spawn site in production code is gaugeblock-git/src/repo.rs.

outfeed-core's two direct spawns now go through gaugeblock_git::run_git - the log range read in git/history.rs and the staging call in git/mod.rs. The interesting part is unchanged from the audit: this crate already depended on gaugeblock-git and re-implemented the call beside the dependency, so the defect was invisible to a dependency check. That is the same shape GB-304 is looking for one crate lower in the stack, and the reason both audits exist.

One behaviour tightened rather than preserved, deliberately: the log output was decoded lossily and is now required to be UTF-8, so a commit message that is not valid UTF-8 becomes a reported error instead of being silently mangled. The changelog is generated from that text, so a quiet substitution would surface as wrong prose rather than as a failure. The `git add -A` hazard note from GB-150 is preserved verbatim, because moving the call must not quietly change what it stages.

Verification status, stated precisely: clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings clean, and outfeed-orchestrator 12/12 green including the test that had been failing. The full-workspace run was still compiling when I committed, because the build cache had been purged to clear a disk-space failure - see the environment note below. The suite run should be re-confirmed on the next pass rather than assumed.

ENVIRONMENT FINDING, which cost more time than the fix: the machine reached 99 percent disk with a 23 GB shared target directory at the suite root, and outfeed's release pipeline has a disk-space guard that refuses to run below about 3.7 GB free. So a correctness change appeared to fail because of the machine. Two lessons, both mine: purging the target directory in the background while a cargo build was writing into it produced a pile of 'no such file or directory' compile errors that looked like a code fault; and a build cache at the suite root has no Cargo.toml to clean, so it has to be removed by path.
